routeHint: Requires Settings -> Modules -> Projects -> Enable Project Management to be ON for this tenant. Then sidebar -> PROJECTS section -> click the section title, or go to /projects directly.
alt: Projects page showing Active and Archived tabs and project cards with a coloured dot, owner avatar and completed task count
notes: Four active projects plus one archived are seeded, so the Active tab shows a 4 count, the Archived tab a 1 count, and every card carries its own colour, owner avatar and a completed/total task ratio.

routeHint: Projects list -> open the project that has tasks -> Overview tab. The id in the URL is the project uuid, a 26 character base32 string, not a numeric id.
alt: Project Overview tab with status and priority pie charts, a needs attention panel, recent tasks and a team workload list
notes: Recapture after the task due-date reseed: the Needs attention panel used to read 7 overdue because every seeded due date was in the past.

routeHint: Open the project -> cog icon labelled Settings in the project header -> Members in the left settings nav. Must be signed in as ADMIN_TENANT or the project owner, otherwise the cog is hidden. 2026-11-11: /project/<uuid>/settings now redirects to settings/general (router.js:1539) and the sections are general, objectives, workflow and members (router.js:1542). The old click on .settings-nav-item:nth-child(2) landed on workflow, and Individual members / Add specific users no longer exist: components/Project/Settings/ProjectSettingsMembers.vue is one People with access card (owner, groups and individuals together, each with a role, Add button). Route now points straight at settings/members, actions removed, waitFor text=People with access. The People with access card was empty apart from the owner, so project 10 was seeded with two groups and three people (project_group (10,15683) Executive and (10,15669) Finance Committee; project.group_roles '{"15683": "admin", "15669": "member"}'; project_user rows for Amelia Whitfield 209225 contributor, Jonas Vargas 209202 member, Liam Dubois 209249 viewer, added_by 207128, tenant 282).
alt: Project settings on the Members section: the People with access card listing the owner, two groups and three individual people each with a role and an Add button, above a table of what each role can do
notes: `click text=Members` matched the wrong node and left the General tab on screen, so the previous shot was of the tab before the click. The settings nav is three sibling buttons; the second is Members. Seven individual members are seeded, otherwise the pane renders the 'No individual members added' empty state.

routeHint: Goals must be enabled first: project Settings -> General -> Project options -> tick Goals and save. Objectives are a separate switch on the project. Seed at least one objective and two goals before capture. UPDATED 2026-11-11: project 10 had objectives_enabled = 0, so the settings sidebar offered only General, Statuses & types and Members and this route fell back to General. The flag is on now. The three objectives are the seeded ones, Grow Membership, Improve Engagement and Financial Sustainability; the old waitFor named 'Grow and retain the membership', which never existed in this data. Second correction the same day: the client reads project.settings.hasGoals (utils/projectFilters.js:98), not the objectives_enabled column, so setting the column alone changed nothing and the route kept falling back to General. Both are set now, and the route is the explicit /settings/objectives.
alt: The Objectives section of project settings, listing the project objectives with their colour and how many tasks each one holds
notes: Goals.vue only renders objective sections when the project has objectives enabled, and the Add objective button lives inside that same branch. Two objectives are seeded, one holding two goals and one holding two.

alt: Projects module settings with the Enable Project Management switch turned on and its helper text
notes: Full-page capture put a 60px strip of content at the top of an otherwise empty 2160px frame. Cropping to .module-layout-with-menu keeps the module header and the Configuration menu alongside the switch and drops the dead space.

routeHint: Open the project -> Tasks tab. Capture with no filters applied so the assignee avatar row, Group by, Status and Columns controls are all visible.
alt: Project Tasks tab with assignee avatars, group by and status filters, and a table of tasks with status and priority tags
notes: The avatar filter row is built from /search-project-user, which returns the project owner plus individual project members. With no project_user rows it showed a single avatar; seven members are now seeded. Created dates are spread across ten weeks instead of all landing on one day.

routeHint: Open the project -> Tasks tab -> Add task. Type a title and add two checklist items so the modal is not empty, but do not save. 2026-11-11: there is no task modal any more. Add task (or C) opens an inline row at the top of the list (components/Project/TaskList/TaskQuickAdd.vue, input .tl-qa-in) with chips for status, priority, assignee and type; the title field understands !high, @name and #type tokens, and checklist, description and comments are filled afterwards in the task panel (see platform/tasks.mdx, Creating a task). The old fill .modal-input input, .o-comment-area textarea and checklist actions had nothing to match. The shot now shows the open row with the title and a !high token typed and nothing submitted, so no task is created. The file name still says modal; the new image is the inline form. Renamed from task-form-modal on 2026-11-11: there is no task modal any more, so both the spec id and the image name said something the screen does not do.
actions: fill .tl-qa-in | Book the venue for the November AGM !high
alt: Tasks tab with the new-task row open above the list: the title Book the venue for the November AGM typed in, with To Do, High, Assignee and Type chips beneath it and the Enter and Esc hints on the right
notes: The Goal row only renders when the project has hasGoals in its settings, which is now on. The three fill actions in the old spec used a space instead of the runner's selector|value separator, so all three were skipped and the modal was captured empty. The b-tooltip on the Checklist header pops open while the pointer sits there after the last click, so the pointer is parked on the modal title before the shot.

routeHint: Open the project -> Board tab. Best with tasks spread across To do, In Progress and Done. 2026-11-11: the board has no Columns button any more; the header is Assignee, Type and Swimlanes (diagnose on the strategic plan board). Closed columns now start collapsed to a narrow Done strip, which expands on click and lists tasks completed in the last 7 days (older ones sit behind Show all). Route moved from the Strategic Plan project (1108bh1kjj83rp1imlj04kkm9m, whose open tasks are mostly one column) to Autumn Conference 2026 (2208bh1kjj83rp1imlj04kkm9n, project 13), the demo project seeded on 2026-11-11 with tasks in every column, including the Negotiate venue for the autumn conference card the waitFor names. The Done task had date_completed NULL, so it counted as old and the expanded column was empty; seeded UPDATE task SET date_completed='2026-11-08 10:00:00' WHERE project_id=13 AND tenant_id=282 AND status_id=1939. Action is just click Done. Used on platform/projects.mdx, in the project views section, rather than on tasks.mdx: the board is one of the project's own tabs.
waitFor: text=Negotiate venue for the autumn conference
alt: Project board for Autumn Conference 2026 with four columns, To Do, In Progress, In Review and Done, each holding task cards with a task key, priority icon, type, due date and checklist progress, and Assignee, Type and Swimlanes filters above
notes: ShowBoard.vue moves any open task whose due date is in the past into the Overdue pseudo-column, so with every seeded due date in the past five of six columns were empty. Due dates are now spread: two deliberately overdue, the rest inside the next five weeks. The No status column is hidden through the Columns control so the six columns fit the frame and Done is not clipped; with every task carrying a status that column was empty anyway.

routeHint: Open the project -> Tasks tab -> click a task row that has at least two assignees, a checklist and one comment.
alt: Task detail page showing status and type controls, two assignees with a completion counter, a three item checklist and a comment thread
notes: Task 100 (Launch referral campaign) is the showcase row: description, three checklist items with the first ticked, two assignees one of whom has marked their part complete, and a three message comment thread. The app scrolls an inner pane, so fullPage does nothing and a fixed viewport either clips the comments or leaves a third of the frame empty; cropping to .project-layout at the tall viewport keeps the project header and tab row and ends exactly where the card ends.
